entries.description: We pushed a new rule to our traffic filter, the servers handling incoming traffic started maxing out CPU, and everything started returning errors.
symptoms: Servers handling incoming traffic started maxing out CPU

entries.description: Someone was doing routine cleanup, ran a command in the wrong place, and the main database just disappeared.
An operator was taking a few servers out of service, put in the wrong number, and way too many went away at once.
symptoms: Way too many servers went away at once.

entries.description: We found someone had been in our systems for days using old login info from a breach we thought we cleaned up months ago.
symptoms: Unauthorized access to systems using old login information from a breach

entries.description: Our database locked itself to read-only, restarts didn't help, and it turned out some internal counter had hit a hard ceiling.
Network dropped between our two sites for about 40 seconds, the database switched over to the backup on its own, and now both sides have changes the other doesn't have.
symptoms: Network dropped between our two sites for about 40 seconds
Database switched over to the backup on its own
Both sides have changes the other doesn't have

entries.description: Our service registry got sluggish, then write operations started failing, and the whole system fell apart like dominoes.

We deployed a new traffic rule and the servers handling incoming traffic started maxing out CPU and dropping everything, and separately our settings file got pushed everywhere at once and broke the whole network.
symptoms: servers handling incoming traffic started maxing out CPU
settings file got pushed everywhere at once

entries.description: An operator ran the wrong command during maintenance and deleted our main database, and in a separate incident someone put in the wrong parameter while removing servers and took down way more capacity than intended.
symptoms: Way more capacity than intended taken down

entries.description: We pushed a security update to all our Windows machines, and every single one of them crashed and blue-screened at the same time.
We rotated our cloud storage keys following the playbook, and now nothing can authenticate even though we did everything right.
We found someone had been in our systems for days using old login info, and our nightly finance reports stopped generating and the numbers coming out are wrong.
Our database locked itself to read-only and some internal counter had hit a hard ceiling, and the office badge readers stopped working so nobody could get into the building.
symptoms: some internal counter had hit a hard ceiling

entries.description: Our nightly reports stopped generating, the finance team says last month's numbers are wrong, and nobody changed anything as far as we know.
symptoms: Finance team says last month's numbers are wrong

entries.description: The air conditioning in the server room failed over the weekend, a few machines shut themselves down from the heat, and one of them hasn't come back up.
symptoms: one machine hasn't come back up
